directAnswer: Yes, USB-C can carry video signals, provided the device supports DisplayPort or HDMI Alt Mode.
summary: USB-C is a versatile connector that can transmit video, audio, and power. However, not all USB-C ports support video output.

sections.heading: USB-C Video Support
sections.body: USB-C ports can support video output through protocols like DisplayPort Alt Mode or HDMI Alt Mode. Check your device specifications to confirm support.

sections.heading: Device Compatibility
sections.body: Ensure both your source device (like a laptop or smartphone) and the display (monitor or TV) support video over USB-C. Adapters may be required for compatibility.

sections.heading: Common Adapters
sections.body: To connect USB-C to HDMI or DisplayPort displays, use an appropriate adapter. Be sure to select one that supports the required video resolution.

steps.title: Check Device Specifications
steps.detail: Verify if your device's USB-C port supports video output by checking the manufacturer's specifications or user manual.

steps.title: Select the Right Adapter
steps.detail: Choose an adapter that supports the video output format you need, such as HDMI or DisplayPort.

steps.title: Connect and Configure
steps.detail: Connect your USB-C device to the display using the adapter, then configure display settings in your operating system to extend or mirror the display.

faqs.question: Can I use a regular USB-C cable for video?
faqs.answer: Not all USB-C cables support video; ensure your cable is rated for video transmission.

faqs.question: What resolutions can USB-C support for video?
faqs.answer: USB-C can support resolutions up to 4K and beyond, depending on the specifications of the device and the cable used.

faqs.question: Will USB-C work with older HDMI devices?
faqs.answer: Yes, but you will need a USB-C to HDMI adapter to connect to older HDMI devices.

caveats: Not all USB-C ports support video output; check device specifications.
